; core.fk - direct Form core stdlib.
;
; This file is executable by the current `fkwu --src` reader. The older BML
; class surface still lives at surface/core.fk as the high-grammar reference;
; this executable core keeps the same public vocabulary while carrying the
; Num/List/Cell/Task abstraction as inspectable Form data.
;
; Do not define wrappers for primitive structural operators such as head, tail,
; len, nth, cons, list, or empty here. Keeping those primitive names unshadowed
; lets source witnesses use the kernel's direct access paths.

(do
    (defn identity (x) x)

    ; The string "narrow waist" — str_len / str_byte_at / byte_to_str (plus
    ; str_concat) are the native composition floor for string behavior built in
    ; Form: measure, decompose (one raw byte, 0-255), construct (the exact
    ; dual), join. str_eq remains an orthogonal compare primitive. Confirmed
    ; present, byte-identical, on fkwu, Go,
    ; Rust, and TS (receipts/2026-07-01-narrow-waist-string-cleanup.md).
    ; Everything below is Form composition over that floor — substring,
    ; char_at, ord, int_to_str — kept as the portable fallback shape. The
    ; kernel dispatch override is intentionally narrow: byte-string/cursor
    ; waist names stay native when same-named fallback definitions are loaded,
    ; so source compilers and cursors keep byte indexing instead of accidentally
    ; routing through slower fallback string reconstruction. Other same-named
    ; Form bindings remain ordinary user definitions.

    (defn fstr-substring-loop (s i end acc)
        (if (ge i end) acc
            (fstr-substring-loop s (add i 1) end (str_concat acc (byte_to_str (str_byte_at s i))))))
    (defn substring (s start end) (fstr-substring-loop s start end ""))

    (defn char_at (s i) (substring s i (add i 1)))
    (defn ord (c) (if (eq (str_len c) 0) -1 (str_byte_at c 0)))

    ; int_to_str — decimal rendering, built from byte_to_str + arithmetic
    ; (ASCII '0' is byte 48), not a digit-l
source_tail:
(let emit (rule-reverse-emitter rule))
            (emit object)))

    (defn bmf-roundtrip (rule source)
        (do
            (let first-match (apply-object-rule rule source))
            (let first-object (cap-get (match-caps first-match) "result"))
            (let reverse-source (apply-object-rule-reverse rule first-object))
            (let second-match (apply-object-rule rule reverse-source))
            (let second-object (cap-get (match-caps second-match) "result"))
            (list "bmf-roundtrip"
                  first-object
                  reverse-source
                  second-object)))

    (defn bmf-roundtrip-first-object (rt) (nth rt 1))
    (defn bmf-roundtrip-source (rt) (nth rt 2))
    (defn bmf-roundtrip-second-object (rt) (nth rt 3))

    (defn bmf-roundtrip-node-eq? (rt)
        (node_eq (bmf-object-value (bmf-roundtrip-first-object rt))
                 (bmf-object-value (bmf-roundtrip-second-object rt))))

    0)

; runtime-grammar.fk - dynamic grammar registry and discovery.
;
; This module sits above engine.fk. The engine owns BMF object matching and
; reversible rule execution; this module owns runtime discovery, selector
; registration, and config-driven loading policy.

(walk_recipe_here (read_form_binary "form-stdlib/.cache/source-compiled/.b17b953e0c365983-333866e9c5dac7d9.OpGxQ7.form.action.fkb"))

; runtime-grammar-selector-registry-band.fk - config-driven grammar selection.
;
; Runtime code reads an extension-to-grammar config file, loads the grammar
; file named by that config, registers the grammar plugin, and routes a source
; file by its filename extension. This proof does not preload or name any
; specific language grammar.
;
; preludes: form-stdlib/core.fk form-stdlib/json.fk form-stdlib/cache.fk form-stdlib/form-ontology-loader.fk form-stdlib/engine.fk form-stdlib/runtime-grammar.fk
